Convert a parsed library to standard NIST MSP format

convert_to_nist_msp.Rd

One-time conversion of any in-house library (Bruker .library or CSU-PMF .mspLib) to a clean NIST MSP file suitable for Zenodo deposition and downstream use with import_msp.

What this function does:

  • Normalizes field names to NIST standard (IonPolarity: pos → Ion_mode: POSITIVE, InstName → Instrument, etc.)

  • Decodes CSU-PMF SYNON codes to proper fields ($:11Pos → Ion_mode: POSITIVE, $:05 → RetentionTime, etc.)

  • Infers Spectrum_type: MS1 when the SYNON $:00 value is in-source and no MSMS field is present

  • Calculates ExactMass from Formula via calculate_exact_mass if absent (common in Bruker files)

  • Writes peaks one pair per line (NIST standard)

  • Drops Bruker-specific internal fields (ReserveDWord, AnalName, BasePeak, PeakWidth, etc.)

  • Skips optional identifiers (InChIKey, InChI, SMILES) if absent — entries do not need to match MoNA completeness

Usage

convert_to_nist_msp(
  library,
  output_path,
  source_lab = NULL,
  source_instrument = NULL
)

Arguments

library

A parsed library list — output of read_library.

output_path

Path for the output .msp file.

source_lab

Optional contributor/lab name appended to Comments: (e.g. "Your Lab, Your University").

source_instrument

Optional fallback instrument string used when no instrument field is present in an entry.

Value

Invisibly returns output_path.

Details

Three-step workflow:

  1. read_library — tolerates any MSP-like format

  2. convert_to_nist_msp — one-time normalization; run once and save the resulting .msp for all future use

  3. import_msp — strict NIST MSP importer with filtering, entropy QC, and deduplication for downstream analysis

See also

read_library, import_msp, calculate_exact_mass

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# ---- Bruker .library → NIST MSP ----
bruker_raw <- read_library("inhouse_library.library")
convert_to_nist_msp(bruker_raw, "inhouse_library.msp",
                    source_lab = "Your Lab, Your University")

# ---- CSU-PMF .mspLib → NIST MSP ----
csu_raw <- read_library("CSUPMF_C8_lib.mspLib")
convert_to_nist_msp(csu_raw, "CSUPMF_C8.msp",
                    source_lab = "Broeckling Lab, Colorado State University")

# ---- From now on, always load the clean .msp files via import_msp() ----
inhouse_lib <- import_msp("inhouse_library.msp",
                           spectrum_type = "MS1",
                           dedup_by      = "none")
csu_lib     <- import_msp("CSUPMF_C8.msp",
                           spectrum_type = "MS1",
                           dedup_by      = "none")
} # }
